title: The Digital World Around Us
summary: The digital experiences we use every day depend on physical systems.
objectives: Explain that digital services need physical computers, networks, power, and people.

vocab.def: A tool or experience delivered through connected computers, such as a website or stream.
The physical systems and places that make a service possible.

sections.heading: Start with what you use
sections.body: Videos, messages, online games, school websites, cloud files, and AI tools feel almost instant. They still need real equipment somewhere to receive requests, process information, and send responses.

sections.heading: Not in the air
sections.body: A digital service depends on devices, networks, buildings, electricity, cooling, and people. These connected parts are infrastructure. Learning about infrastructure helps us understand what happens behind a screen.

sections.heading: Think like a systems learner
sections.body: When one part changes, other parts may be affected. Ask: What device is involved? Where might the information travel? What systems keep the computers working?

practice.prompt: Choose one digital service and draw or describe three physical things it needs.

quiz.question: Which statement is accurate?
options: Digital services depend on physical infrastructure
quiz.answer: Digital services depend on physical infrastructure

reflectionPrompt: What digital service do you use most, and what physical system behind it surprised you?
